title: Super funds wary of Firmus leadership ahead of IPO
full_text:
Some major Melbourne-based superannuation funds are planning to swerve the initial public offering of Firmus, sources say, on concerns around the company’s leadership.
While ASIC has assessed Oliver Curtis as a fit and proper person to run the business, sources say some funds remain cautious given his history – including a period of incarceration for insider trading – which they say falls outside their governance risk settings for new investments.
The Firmus IPO plans continue to ramp up, with five retail brokers on the ticket looking to sell the artificial-intelligence hopeful that is yet to provide any details surrounding its earnings or customer contracts.
There is talk that it hopes to embark on a $4bn IPO to have a $15bn market value and that it will suggest it will make more than $4bn in earnings before interest and tax this year – numbers that have been met with scepticism.
Sources said the company that was yet to generate any meaningful revenue wanted to target a valuation of 15 times forecast EBIT. A recent $2.9bn equity placement values Firmus at $15.5bn.
